previousIssues.status: fixed. The seat renders at about 0.6 of the lining. m13 seat (260,350) #6e6e6f and pedestal (250,480) #59595a, against lining (100,300) #bbbab5. m18 seat (345,320) #7c7d7f, against lining (450,250) #b8b6b1. That is close to lalf_133's 0.5. The straps still read as blue-grey metal rods (m17 x 460/510), but this is minor.

previousIssues.issue: w9b MEDIUM / w9a MEDIUM: galley beverage makers were wide black blocks with a stacked-cup cylinder
previousIssues.status: partly fixed. The black block is gone. There is now a satin head, a black control strip with a green key, a lathed jug with a black lid and handle, and a drip tray, which is clearly the right product family (m09, m01, m12, q19). Three things remain, and they are carried forward as a new medium. (1) Each brewer is a single unit across the full ~0.33 m insert, with a small jug in a wide bay. sans_38 and sansY_44 show two narrow brewers per bay, with the jug filling each one. (2) The head and the 0.12 m deep cheeks stand about 8 cm proud of the ovens, so the bay reads as a box with an open side door (m09 x 610-665, m19 x 820-930). (3) The jug renders flat mid-grey, where the real one is polished, high-contrast stainless.

previousIssues.issue: w9b MEDIUM (a): welcome glass cabinet pane opaque; w9a MEDIUM: reads as a panelled door
previousIssues.status: partly fixed in the rendered head, and a fix is in progress. In the w10 renders the shelves and boxes show through, so it no longer reads as a door. However, the two narrow upright sheen strips render as pale bars from top to bottom, and the cabinet reads as a display cage (m16 x~690 and ~800, m03 (715,300) #4e4a45 against #2c2927 beside it). The working tree (uncommitted diff in 10_mono.js) already replaces the strips with a glossy pane plus silhouettes. See the issue below for the risk that this reverts to the w9 painted-door look.

issues.detail: Galley beverage makers (m09, m01, m12, q19, m19)
issues.problem: The brewers are now the right product family, but three things still mark them as wrong at a glance. (1) Each brewer spans the whole ~0.33 m insert, with one small jug in a wide bay. In sans_38 and sansY_44, two narrow brewers sit side by side in one insert slot, and each jug fills its bay. (2) The head (0.12 deep) and side cheeks (0.12 deep) stand about 8 cm proud of the oven doors, which are 0.04 deep. The right cheek therefore reads as an open side door, and the head as a box bolted onto the face. This is most visible in m09 (x 610-665), m19 (x 820-930) and m12 (x 95-230). (3) The jug renders as flat mid-grey. The real jugs are polished stainless with a very wide value range, from near-black reflections to bright highlights.
issues.evidence: m09 jug (575,355) #474847 and (560,330) #555656; cheek (640,350) #2c2b29. sansY_44 jug highlight (890,120) #bdbaa7 and (900,160) #a8a38d against reflection (720,150) #1a180c. sans_38 jug (770,240) #767360. In sans_38 (660-890, 105-305), three brewer frames sit in about the width of one oven.
issues.fix: In brewer() (10_mono.js ~l.182): (1) Reduce the depths. Head gRBox(uW, 0.13, 0.05, 0.01, 1) at P(0, y0+0.165, 0.025); control strip and window at oo 0.051-0.052; brew handle at oo 0.06. Cheeks gBox(0.014, 0.21, 0.05) at oo 0.025; drip tray gBox(uW-0.03, 0.01, 0.06) at oo 0.035. Jug and handle at oo 0.035, so the jug belly (r 0.06) sits just proud of the frame, as in sansY_44. (2) In buildGalley t===1, call brewer twice: for (const s of [-1,1]) brewer(B, (dx,y,oo) => G(dx + s*uW/4, y, o+oo), uW/2 - 0.01, 1.41). Scale the jug lathe radii by 0.8 for the narrow bay. (3) MONMAT.jug: { c: '#c4c2bc', r: 0.15, m: 0.35 } so the diffuse carries the tone. Add one baked highlight down the jug front: gBox(0.01, 0.07, 0.002) at P(-0.02, y0-0.05, 0.035+0.06) in { c: '#eceae4', r: 0.1, e: 0.25 }, plus a dark reflection strip gBox(0.012, 0.07, 0.002) at dx +0.02 in '#1d1c1a'.

issues.problem: In the rendered head (ed77bfe), the two upright sheen strips read as pale vertical bars across the whole pane (m16 x~690 and ~800, m03 x 635 and 715), so the cabinet looks like a cage or a display case with rods. The uncommitted working-tree change replaces the strips with an opaque glossy pane (#2f2c2a, m 0.35) and silhouette quads drawn on it. That removes the bars, but it risks going back to the w9 'painted taupe door' look: an opaque pane with low-contrast silhouettes, and the interior shelves and boxes behind it never drawn. In omaat_room_32 and lalf_134 the pane is dark but the contents show at good contrast: a pale interior wall, papers and a lit shelf edge.
issues.evidence: m03 (715,300) #4e4a45 and (635,300) #2c2927 (strips). m16 (690,300) #302d2b, (800,300) #232220. Interior m16 (760,250) #1f1d1b. omaat_room_32 pane contents p90 ~#82 (brief w9); lalf_134 pane (960,450) #614d4f with a pale interior.
issues.fix: Keep the new single pane quad, but make what shows through readable. In the silhouette list, raise the brightest boxes and papers to about #7a766e / #8a867e, and add a pale back-wall quad behind them (gQuad(0.32, 0.66) at o+0.0882, { c: '#4a4744', r: 0.1, m: 0.2 }) so that the silhouettes, at o+0.0884, sit on a lighter ground than the frame. Keep the pane at r 0.05 so the downlight reflections sell the glass. Add one soft diagonal reflection only, gQuad(0.06, 0.70) rotated ~0.25 rad, { c: '#5a5652', r: 0.05, m: 0.3 }, at o+0.0886, and no upright full-height strips. Check m16 for bars before committing.

issues.problem: Unchanged. The bottles are fat bullets: a cone runs straight to the top with no neck or cap. Eight are packed with touching bodies (r 0.036 at ~0.06 m pitch), and they are opaque grey. In samchui_render_11, five or six slim clear bottles stand with gaps, with long necks, caps and white labels.
issues.evidence: m05 bottle (690,330) #57686e and (660,360) #364248. Fridge bottles (830,200) #57686e. samchui_render_11 bottle shine (610,320) #e8e8e8.
issues.fix: bottle(): body gCyl(r, r, h*0.6) at h*0.3; shoulder gCyl(r*0.4, r, h*0.12) at h*0.66; neck gCyl(r*0.3, r*0.3, h*0.2) at h*0.82; cap gCyl(r*0.34, r*0.34, h*0.05) at h*0.945 in MONMAT.black. In buildBar, draw 6 shelf bottles (k<6) at r 0.028 so there are gaps, and lighten bottleClear to { c: '#c9d6da', r: 0.05, m: 0.15, e: 0.04 }.

issues.detail: Welcome monitor stands proud of the tower (m16)
issues.problem: The welcome screen is drawn as a separate slab about 6 cm in front of the tower face, with visible side thickness and a gap above the bays. In lalf_134 and omaat_room_32 the screen sits in a flush dark bezel that is part of the tower, with the shelf lip below it.
issues.evidence: m16 monitor x 290-510, y 105-325: side thickness visible at x 500-510. lalf_134 (660-880, 250-520) is flush.
issues.fix: In buildWelcomeGalley, move the bezel gRBox(0.90, 0.54, 0.03) to o+0.008 and the screen quad to o+0.024. Add a welcomeChar frame ring (four gBox strips, 0.03 wide, depth 0.03 at o+0.015) round it so the tower reads as one carcass.

issues.problem: The latches render dark brick-red. The real ones are orange-brown anodised, with bright orange highlights.
issues.fix: MONMAT.copper: { c: '#b5643a', r: 0.3, m: 0.35 }, which is less red and keeps more of the diffuse.

issues.problem: The PY bassinet steel bar (m08) and the m04 flap seam and square frames are unchanged. The q01 ebony grain has harsh long streaks. The bar blind is darker than the render, and the upper galley units have a dark gradient band; both are lighting hand-offs.
issues.fix: Bassinet: in buildBulkhead, replace gRBox(0.3, 0.03, 0.02) with two gCyl(0.018, 0.018, 0.01, 12) discs at x±0.15, rotated to face the cabin, in '#2a2a2e'. Ash wall: as in w9b (a single gRBox frame behind each flap; flap at F(x, 1.28, 0.01)). Blind: MONMAT.blind c '#4a4950', or e 0.02. Gradient: lighting area.
